subject: Civil Engineering
title: What Dams Do
description: A quick, practical guide to What Dams Do.

hook.text: A dam blocks a river — storing billions of gallons for drinking, farming, and electricity.

buildup.text: Dams control floods by holding back storm water and releasing it slowly downstream.

discovery.text: Hydropower dams convert falling water into electricity — about 16% of global generation.

twist.text: Dams also create ecosystems — reservoirs become fisheries, wetlands, and recreation areas.

climax.text: Over 58,000 large dams exist worldwide — storing 15% of the world's annual river runoff.

punchline.text: A wall across a river changes everything downstream — water, power, and life.

quiz.question: What percentage of global electricity comes from hydropower dams?

details.summary: Dams are barriers built across rivers to impound water for irrigation, drinking supply, flood control, hydropower generation, and recreation. By regulating natural river flow, dams store water during wet periods and release it during dry periods.
details.whyItMatters: Dams provide water supply to over 40% of the world's irrigated farmland and generate roughly 16% of global electricity. They are among the most consequential structures humans build.
takeaways: Dams serve multiple purposes including water supply, flood control, and power generation
Reservoirs store surplus water for release during dry seasons and droughts
Over 58,000 large dams exist worldwide, most built in the twentieth century

faq.question: What is the difference between a dam and a reservoir?
faq.answer: A dam is the physical barrier structure built across a waterway. A reservoir is the body of water that accumulates behind the dam. The dam creates the reservoir.

faq.question: How do multi-purpose dams balance competing water uses?
faq.answer: Operators follow rule curves that specify reservoir levels for each season. Flood storage is kept empty to absorb storm inflows. Water supply storage is maintained for dry periods. Hydropower generation is scheduled to match electricity demand.
